segments.text: Euclid's Elements, Book One, Proposition Two. Construct at a given point a segment equal to a given segment. Given point A and segment B C, we are to construct at point A a segment equal to B C.

subsegments.text: Euclid's Elements, Book One, Proposition Two. Construct at a given point a segment equal to a given segment. Given point A and segment B C, we are to construct at point A a segment equal to B C.

segments.style: speaking briskly, nimble, crisp, and composed
segments.text: From point A to point B, construct segment A B. On segment A B, construct the equilateral triangle D A B. Next, extend segments D A and D B continuously to E and F. Construct circle B C, with center B and defining radius point C, intersecting D F at G. Next, construct circle D G, with center D and defining radius point G, intersecting D E at L.

subsegments.text: From point A to point B, construct segment A B. On segment A B, construct the equilateral triangle D A B. Next, extend segments D A and D B continuously to E and F. Construct circle B C, with center B and defining radius point C, intersecting D F at G. Next, construct circle D G, with center D and defining radius point G, intersecting D E at L.

segments.style: speaking briskly, nimble, crisp, and composed
segments.text: Since B is the center of circle B C, segment B C equals segment B G. Again, since D is the center of circle D G, segment D L equals segment D G. Within these, D A equals D B from our equilateral triangle, so subtracting equals from equals, the remainder A L equals the remainder B G. Because both A L and B C equal B G, things equal to the same thing are equal to one another. Therefore segment A L equals segment B C, and has been constructed at the given point A, as was required to do.
